# Section 23 09 93 – Sequence of Operations: Central Chilled Water Plant

This is drafted in spec format for you to edit into the BAS specification. Bracketed values `[ ]` are starting values the operator can adjust. Confirm them with the chiller manufacturer, the TAB contractor and the engineer of record. Coordination items and assumptions are listed at the end in Section 15. Several of them affect how the sequence works and should be resolved before bid.

---

## 1. General

1.1 **Scope.** This sequence covers chillers CH-1/2/3, primary chilled water pumps CHWP-1/2/3, bypass valve FCV-701, primary flow meter FIT-702, cooling towers CT-1/2/3, condenser water pumps CWP-1/2/3, and the associated isolation valves, sensors and alarms.

1.2 **Design intent.**
- a. Variable primary flow plant serving a hospital, including surgery suites that must not lose cooling.
- b. N+1 redundancy: the design load must be met with any one chiller, primary pump, condenser pump or tower cell out of service. Firm plant capacity is 1,600 tons, from two chillers at 800 tons each.
- c. Reliability takes priority over energy optimization. Where the two conflict, this sequence favors continuity of cooling.

1.3 **Control hierarchy.**
- a. Each chiller's onboard controls handle its own safeties, capacity control to the CHWST setpoint, and its own anti-recycle timers.
- b. The BAS handles enabling and staging, pumps, valves, towers, setpoint reset, and alarms.
- c. The BAS writes these points to each chiller through the [BACnet/IP] interface: enable/disable, CHWST setpoint, and demand limit.
- d. Hardwired points to each chiller are required: chiller run/enable, chiller run status, and common alarm. Network points supplement the hardwired points and do not replace them.

1.4 **Equipment availability.** A device is "available" only when all of these are true:
- a. Its HOA or local/remote switch is in Auto/Remote.
- b. It has no active fault or lockout.
- c. Its VFD is not faulted.
- d. The operator has not taken it out of service at the graphic.

The BAS uses only available equipment for staging and failover.

1.5 **Lead/lag rotation.**
- a. Chillers, CHWPs, CWPs and tower cells rotate their lead/lag order [weekly, Monday 10:00]. Equipment with the fewest run hours becomes lead.
- b. Rotation never stops a running unit. The new order takes effect at the next staging event.
- c. The operator can manually fix the lead order.
- d. Rotation is inhibited while any surgery suite AHU is in occupied mode, if the owner selects this option. Otherwise it occurs during the scheduled window only.

1.6 **Global timers** (all adjustable):

| Parameter | Default |
|---|---|
| Chiller minimum run time | [30 min] |
| Chiller minimum off time | [15 min], or manufacturer anti-recycle, whichever is longer |
| Stage-up delay | [10 min] |
| Stage-down delay | [15 min] |
| Interstage delay (any stage change to next stage change) | [15 min] |
| Flow-proving delay | [60 s] |

---

## 2. Plant Enable / Disable

2.1 **Normal mode.** The chilled water plant is enabled continuously, 24/7/365.
- a. Hospital cooling loads, including surgery, imaging, IT/telecom and pharmacy, require year-round chilled water.
- b. There is no outdoor air lockout.

2.2 **Operator disable.** The plant can be disabled only through a password-protected graphic command at the highest access level.
- a. The command requires a confirmation dialog.
- b. Disabling the plant generates a critical alarm.

2.3 **Low-load operation.** When the load is below one chiller's minimum stable capacity, the lead chiller remains enabled.
- a. The chiller cycles on its own controls, subject to its anti-recycle timer.
- b. The bypass valve maintains minimum flow per Section 5.

---

## 3. Chiller Staging

3.1 **Minimum chillers operating.**
- a. An operator-adjustable parameter sets the minimum number of chillers operating.
- b. Default: [1].
- c. **Owner option:** set this to 2 during surgery suite occupied hours, or continuously. This provides hot standby. If one chiller trips, the second is already running and carrying load, so there is no restart gap.
- d. This uses more energy, but it is the most robust way to prevent a cooling interruption to the ORs. The owner's decision should be recorded in the BOD.

3.2 **Plant load calculation.**
- a. Plant load (tons) = FIT-702 flow (gpm) × (CHWRT − CHWST) (°F) / 24.
- b. CHWRT is the common return temperature. CHWST is the common supply temperature. Both sensors must be matched-pair, ±0.1°F (see Section 15).
- c. The calculated load is filtered over a [5 min] rolling average.

3.3 **Stage up.** The BAS enables the next available chiller when any of the following conditions is true for the stage-up delay:
- a. Common CHWST is more than [1.5°F] above the active setpoint.
- b. Average %RLA (or % kW) of the operating chillers exceeds [90%].
- c. Calculated plant load exceeds [90%] of the operating chillers' combined capacity.
- d. Flow per operating chiller exceeds [1,700 gpm], which is about 106% of design. Use the per-chiller evaporator ΔP converted to flow, or FIT-702 divided by the number of chillers.
- e. **Immediate stage-up, with no delay:** an operating chiller trips or fails to prove run within [5 min] of enable. See Section 10.

3.4 **Stage down.** The BAS disables the lag chiller when all of the following conditions are true for the stage-down delay:
- a. Calculated plant load is below [70%] of the capacity of the chillers that would remain after stage-down.
- b. Common CHWST is within [0.5°F] of setpoint.
- c. The minimum chillers operating parameter (3.1) would still be satisfied.
- d. The chiller's minimum run time has elapsed.

3.5 **Stage-up procedure (variable primary transition).** This procedure limits flow disturbance to the chillers already running.
- a. Command the operating chillers' demand limit to [60%] for [5 min] or until the new chiller proves run, whichever is longer. This prevents the operating chillers from surging or tripping on low leaving temperature when flow is diverted.
- b. Open the incoming chiller's condenser isolation valve. Start the condenser pump per Section 7. Prove condenser flow.
- c. Open the incoming chiller's evaporator isolation valve slowly.
  - i. The stroke time must be [90–120 s], or slower if needed so that flow change through any operating chiller does not exceed the manufacturer's allowable rate. Typical limits are [10–30%] of design flow per minute. **Confirm with the manufacturer.**
- d. Start the additional CHWP per Section 4. Prove evaporator flow by the chiller flow switch and evaporator ΔP.
- e. Enable the tower cell(s) per Section 8.
- f. After the flow-proving delay, enable the chiller.
- g. After the new chiller proves run and reaches [50%] load, or [5 min] pass, release the demand limit on all chillers. The release ramps over [5 min].

3.6 **Stage-down procedure.**
- a. Disable the chiller. Its own controls unload and stop it.
- b. Keep the evaporator and condenser pumps and valves open for the post-run period. Default is [5 min] or per the manufacturer.
- c. Close the evaporator isolation valve slowly, using the same rate as 3.5c.
- d. Stop the excess CHWP. Close the condenser valve and stop the CWP. Disable the excess tower cell(s).

3.7 **Redundancy status.**
- a. The BAS continuously evaluates whether the plant has N+1 capability. The plant has N+1 when the available chillers, minus the largest single chiller, can meet the current calculated load plus [10%].
- b. If the plant does not have N+1 capability, the BAS displays **"PLANT OPERATING WITHOUT REDUNDANCY"** on the plant graphic and generates a high-priority alarm. The same applies to pumps and tower cells.
- c. The BAS also alarms when all three chillers are running, because at that point there is no standby.

---

## 4. Primary Chilled Water Pumps (CHWP-1/2/3)

4.1 **Pump count.** The pumps are headered.
- a. The number of pumps running equals the number of chillers running, with a minimum of one.
- b. Pumps are not tied to specific chillers. Any available pump can serve any chiller.
- c. **Owner option:** the BAS may run one more pump than chillers when the pumps' combined required speed exceeds [90%].

4.2 **Speed control.**
- a. All running pumps operate at the same speed.
- b. A PID loop modulates pump speed to maintain the DPT-710 differential pressure at setpoint.
- c. Setpoint: [12.0 psid].
- d. Minimum speed: [30%], or as determined by TAB as the speed needed to deliver the bypass minimum flow with the bypass valve full open. Use whichever is higher.
- e. Maximum speed: 100%.

4.3 **Redundant DP sensing (recommended).**
- a. Provide a second remote DP sensor, DPT-711, at the most remote surgery suite AHU if that AHU is not the one DPT-710 serves.
- b. The control variable is the lowest of the active DP signals, each compared against its own setpoint. The loop controls to the sensor most below its setpoint.
- c. If any one DP sensor fails, the BAS uses the remaining sensor(s).

4.4 **DP sensor failure.** A DP signal is failed if it is out of range, or if it reads 0 psid with pumps proven running for [2 min].
- a. If all remote DP signals are failed, the BAS holds pump speed at [last good value, but not less than 80%].
- b. The BAS generates a high-priority alarm.

4.5 **Plant DP high limit.**
- a. A plant-header DP sensor (DPT-712) overrides pump speed downward if header DP exceeds [design + 10 psi].
- b. This protects piping and coil valves from excess pressure when loads are low.

4.6 **Pump staging transitions.**
- a. When a pump starts, it ramps from minimum speed to match the running pump speed over [30 s].
- b. When a pump stops, the remaining pumps ramp to absorb its flow.

4.7 **Pump failure.**
- a. If a running pump fails to prove status (current switch or VFD run feedback) within [15 s] of command, or loses status while running, the BAS takes these steps:
  - i. Generates an alarm.
  - ii. Locks out the failed pump.
  - iii. Starts the next available pump immediately.
- b. This action does not stop or wait on any chiller.

---

## 5. Minimum Flow Bypass (FCV-701)

5.1 **Purpose.** The bypass maintains flow through the operating chillers at or above their minimum.

5.2 **Minimum flow setpoint.**
- a. Minimum flow setpoint (gpm) = (number of chillers proven running) × 960 gpm × [1.10] safety factor.
- b. This works out to [1,056 / 2,112 / 3,168 gpm] for one, two or three chillers.

5.3 **Control.**
- a. FCV-701 is normally closed.
- b. A PID loop modulates FCV-701 open as needed to keep chiller flow (FIT-702) at or above the minimum flow setpoint.
- c. The valve closes fully when flow exceeds the setpoint by [10%].
- d. The loop uses a fast response. Tune it so that flow does not overshoot below minimum during an AHU valve closure transient.

5.4 **FIT-702 location (critical).**
- a. FIT-702 must measure flow through the chillers. It must be in the primary supply between the chiller header and the bypass tee, or in the return upstream of the bypass tee.
- b. If FIT-702 measures system (load) flow instead, this sequence must be revised. The minimum flow logic changes to "chiller flow = system flow + bypass flow." In that case, a meter in the bypass line or per-chiller flow meters are required.

5.5 **Backup flow indication.**
- a. Each chiller's evaporator ΔP, converted to flow, is trended and compared with FIT-702.
- b. If the two disagree by more than [15%] for [10 min], the BAS generates an alarm.
- c. If FIT-702 fails, the BAS controls the bypass from the sum of the evaporator ΔP-derived flows.
- d. If both FIT-702 and the evaporator ΔP signals fail, FCV-701 goes to a fixed [40%] open position and the BAS generates an alarm.

5.6 **Chiller low-flow protection.**
- a. If any operating chiller's evaporator flow (by evaporator ΔP) falls below [1,000 gpm] for [30 s], the BAS takes these steps:
  - i. Opens FCV-701 to 100%.
  - ii. Increases pump speed by [10%].
  - iii. Generates an alarm.
- b. The chiller's own flow switch remains the final safety.

5.7 **Fail position.** FCV-701 fails [open].
- a. On failure, the pumps speed up to maintain DPT-710, so the system remains served at reduced efficiency.
- b. Chiller minimum flow is protected.
- c. The engineer of record should confirm that the pumps have enough capacity for this condition.

---

## 6. Chilled Water Supply Temperature Setpoint and Reset

6.1 **Base setpoint.** 42.0°F.

6.2 **Reset range.** 42.0°F to 46.0°F maximum.

6.3 **Trim and respond reset.** The BAS evaluates the reset every [5 min] using cooling coil valve positions from all AHUs on the loop.

| Parameter | Default |
|---|---|
| Initial setpoint at reset enable | 42.0°F |
| Request generated when a coil valve is above | [90%] open |
| Ignored requests (excludes rogue zones) | [2] |
| Trim (raise setpoint) if requests ≤ ignored count | +[0.2°F] |
| Respond (lower setpoint) per request above ignored count | −[0.3°F] |
| Maximum respond per interval | −[1.0°F] |

- a. The operator can exclude individual AHUs from the request count from the graphic.
- b. Each excluded AHU is listed on a "reset exclusions" display, so exclusions do not get forgotten.

6.4 **Reset lockouts (hospital-specific).** The CHWST setpoint returns to 42.0°F, ramping down at [0.5°F per 5 min], and the reset is suspended when any of the following conditions is true:
- a. Any surgery suite, procedure room, or other AHU flagged by the owner as critical has its cooling coil valve above [80%].
- b. Any of those AHUs has discharge air temperature more than [1°F] above setpoint for [5 min].
- c. Any of those AHUs has supply air dewpoint above its dewpoint setpoint.
- d. Any OR space RH is above [55%] (ASHRAE 170 upper limit is 60%), or any OR space temperature is above setpoint by [1°F].
- e. Outdoor air dewpoint is above [55°F].
- f. A chiller staging event is in progress, or occurred in the last [15 min].
- g. The plant is operating without redundancy (3.7).
- h. A DPT-710 or DPT-711 failure is active.

6.5 **Basis for lockouts.** ORs commonly require space setpoints of 62–68°F at 20–60% RH. This typically needs supply air of about 50–52°F and coil leaving water near 42–44°F. Raising CHWST can quickly cost OR humidity control, so the lockouts above take priority over energy savings.

6.6 **Pump energy tradeoff.** In variable primary plants, raising CHWST increases chilled water flow and pump energy. The reset benefit should be confirmed during commissioning. The engineer may set the maximum reset below 46°F if trend data shows little or no net savings.

6.7 **Writing the setpoint.** The BAS writes the active setpoint to all operating chillers.
- a. If communication with a chiller is lost, the chiller reverts to its local setpoint.
- b. The local setpoint on each chiller panel must be set to 42.0°F at commissioning.

---

## 7. Condenser Water Pumps (CWP-1/2/3)

7.1 **Configuration.** The pumps are headered, with automatic isolation valves at each chiller condenser. (See Section 15 if the pumps are dedicated.)

7.2 **Pump count.** The number of CWPs running equals the number of chillers enabled.

7.3 **Speed.**
- a. Each CWP runs at a fixed speed setpoint set by TAB to deliver design condenser flow per chiller, [___ gpm].
- b. The VFD is used for balancing and soft start. Variable condenser flow is not used unless the chiller manufacturer approves it in writing.
- c. **Optional:** during chiller startup with cold condenser water, the chiller may request low condenser flow or head pressure control through the BAS interface, per the manufacturer.

7.4 **Proof of flow.**
- a. Condenser flow is proven by the chiller condenser flow switch or condenser ΔP within the flow-proving delay.
- b. If flow is not proven, the BAS takes these steps:
  - i. Generates an alarm.
  - ii. Starts the next available CWP.
  - iii. Retries.
- c. If flow is still not proven after [2] attempts, the BAS locks out the chiller and stages up the next available chiller.

7.5 **Pump failure.** Same response as 4.7.

---

## 8. Cooling Towers (CT-1/2/3)

8.1 **Cell enable.**
- a. The number of tower cells enabled equals the number of chillers running.
- b. **Optional:** enable an additional cell when cell isolation valves and nozzle minimum flow allow it. Running more cells at lower fan speed reduces fan energy. Confirm the tower manufacturer's minimum flow per cell to avoid dry spots and scaling.
- c. For each enabled cell, the BAS opens its inlet and outlet isolation valves before fan enable. The basin equalizer remains open.

8.2 **Condenser water supply temperature (CWST) setpoint.**
- a. CWST setpoint = outdoor wet bulb + [7°F] approach.
- b. The setpoint is limited between [65°F] (or the chiller manufacturer's minimum entering condenser water temperature, whichever is higher) and [85°F].
- c. If the wet bulb calculation fails, the setpoint is fixed at [75°F].

8.3 **Fan control.**
- a. All enabled fans run at the same speed.
- b. A PID loop modulates fan speed to maintain the common CWST at setpoint.
- c. Minimum speed: [20%], or the manufacturer's minimum. Maximum speed: 100%.

8.4 **Low-temperature operation.**
- a. With fans at minimum speed, if CWST is more than [2°F] below setpoint for [5 min], the BAS cycles fans off one at a time. The minimum off time is [5 min].
- b. If CWST remains below the chiller's minimum entering condenser water temperature with all fans off, the BAS modulates the tower bypass valve, if provided. See Section 15.

8.5 **Freeze protection.**
- a. Basin heaters are enabled by their own thermostat when basin temperature is below [40°F] and the basin level is proven.
- b. If outdoor air temperature is below [35°F], the BAS may run fans in reverse for de-icing, if supported, on a schedule of [___].
- c. Heat trace on makeup water and exposed piping is monitored. The BAS alarms on failure.

8.6 **Fan safeties (hardwired at the VFD).**
- a. The vibration switch stops the fan and generates an alarm.
- b. Manual reset is required.

8.7 **Tower cell failure.** On a fan VFD fault, vibration trip, or loss of status, the BAS takes these steps:
- a. Generates an alarm.
- b. Locks out the cell.
- c. Enables the next available cell.

8.8 **Basin level and makeup water.**
- a. The BAS monitors basin level and alarms on high or low level.
- b. On low-low basin level, the BAS generates a critical alarm. The condenser pumps continue to run unless they lose suction, and pump protection is per the manufacturer.

8.9 **Water treatment.**
- a. Water treatment is by others.
- b. The BAS monitors the treatment controller's common alarm, conductivity, and makeup and blowdown meter totals for trending.

---

## 9. Chiller Start / Stop Sequence (Each Chiller)

9.1 **Start.** When the BAS enables a chiller, these steps occur in order:
- a. Open the condenser isolation valve. Prove the open end switch.
- b. Start the CWP if it is not already running. Prove condenser flow.
- c. Open the evaporator isolation valve slowly, per 3.5c. Prove the open end switch.
- d. Start or adjust the CHWP per Section 4. Prove evaporator flow.
- e. Enable the tower cell(s).
- f. After the flow-proving delay, send the chiller enable over the hardwired point and the network.
- g. Prove chiller run status within [5 min]. If run status is not proven, the BAS treats this as a chiller failure (Section 10).

9.2 **Stop.** Follow 3.6.

9.3 **Isolation valve failure.**
- a. If an isolation valve fails to prove its commanded position within [2× stroke time], the BAS generates an alarm.
- b. If the valve was commanded to open, the chiller is treated as unavailable and the next chiller is started.
- c. If the valve was commanded to close and failed to close, the BAS keeps the bypass minimum flow logic active. Flow through the idle chiller dilutes CHWST, so the BAS also generates an alarm with the message "idle chiller flow".

---

## 10. Failure Response and Surgery Suite Protection

10.1 **Chiller trip.** When a running chiller loses run status without a BAS disable command, or its alarm is active, the BAS responds immediately:
- a. Generates a critical alarm.
- b. Locks out the chiller. The operator must reset it at the BAS after the local fault is cleared.
- c. Stages up the next available chiller immediately, using 3.5 with the interstage delay and minimum off time bypassed. The demand limit step 3.5a is skipped for the remaining chillers in this case. They should load up fully.
- d. Releases the demand limit on all running chillers to 100%.
- e. Suspends the CHWST reset per 6.4f.
- f. Commands running CHWPs to maintain DP. The tripped chiller's evaporator valve remains open for the post-run period, then closes.

10.2 **Capacity shortfall.** If CHWST is more than [3°F] above setpoint for [10 min] with all available chillers running, the BAS takes these steps:
- a. Generates a critical alarm.
- b. Sends the **"Chilled Water Capacity Shortfall"** signal to the AHU sequences.
- c. The AHU sequences can use this signal to perform owner-approved load shedding. Load shedding applies to non-critical AHUs only, such as administrative and support areas. Their supply air setpoint is raised or their cooling valves are limited to [70%].
- d. Surgery suites, ICUs, and other spaces flagged as critical are never shed.

10.3 **Sensor failures.**

| Failed sensor | Response |
|---|---|
| Common CHWST | Chillers control to their own leaving temperature at the local setpoint. Reset is disabled. Staging uses %RLA only. Alarm. |
| Common CHWRT | Load calculation is unavailable. Staging uses %RLA and CHWST only. Alarm. |
| FIT-702 | Per 5.5. |
| DPT-710 / DPT-711 | Per 4.3 and 4.4. |
| CWST | Tower fans controlled to the average chiller entering condenser temperature (network point). If that is also unavailable, fans run at fixed [75%]. Alarm. |
| OA wet bulb | Fixed CWST setpoint per 8.2. |

10.4 **BAS controller or network failure.**
- a. **Equipment default states.** Each piece of equipment must default to a state that keeps cooling running:
  - i. Chillers revert to local control and keep running at the local 42°F setpoint, if the hardwired enable was on at the time of failure. The hardwired enable relays must be configured to stay latched, or fail to enabled, for the lead chiller(s). Coordinate details with the engineer.
  - ii. CHWP and CWP VFDs revert to a preset speed of [80% / TAB speed] on loss of BAS command, through the VFD's own loss-of-signal function.
  - iii. Tower fan VFDs revert to preset [75%].
  - iv. FCV-701 fails open.
- b. **Controller architecture.**
  - i. Distribute I/O so that no single controller failure affects more than one chiller, pump or tower train.
  - ii. Plant-level logic, including staging, bypass and DP, resides in a plant controller.
  - iii. **Recommended:** provide a hot-standby redundant plant controller.
- c. **Power for controls.** Plant controllers, network switches, and the plant BAS workstation are on UPS, fed from the essential electrical system. UPS runtime is [30 min] minimum.

10.5 **Utility power failure and emergency power.**
- a. Chillers, pumps and towers are on the essential electrical system (equipment branch), per the electrical design. **Coordinate** this; see Section 15.
- b. On loss of normal power, the BAS records the equipment that was running.
- c. On transfer to generator, equipment restarts in staggered steps to limit generator step loading:
  - i. [0 s]: CHWP(s).
  - ii. [15 s]: CWP(s).
  - iii. [30 s]: tower fans.
  - iv. [60 s]: first chiller.
  - v. [+___ s]: each additional chiller, per generator capacity.
- d. Chillers use their fast-restart feature, if equipped. Anti-recycle timers are bypassed where the manufacturer permits.
- e. The minimum chillers operating parameter (3.1) is respected on restart.
- f. The same staggered restart applies on retransfer to normal power, if equipment drops out during retransfer.

---

## 11. Manual and Override Modes

11.1 **Operator overrides.** The operator can override the following at the graphic, at the appropriate password level:
- a. Chiller enable
- b. Lead/lag order
- c. Pump speed (within the min/max limits)
- d. FCV-701 position
- e. CHWST setpoint (within 40–46°F)
- f. DP setpoint
- g. Tower fan speed

11.2 **Override display.** Every override is displayed on an "Active Overrides" summary page. Each override reverts to Auto after [8 h] unless it is renewed.

11.3 **Hardwired safeties in Hand.** Hand position at the VFD keeps all hardwired safeties active.

---

## 12. Alarms

The BAS annunciates alarms at the workstation. Critical alarms also go to [paging/text/facility alarm system] per the owner's notification matrix.

12.1 **Critical alarms:**
- a. Chiller trip
- b. Capacity shortfall
- c. Plant disabled
- d. Loss of all DP signals
- e. CHWST > [48°F]
- f. Chiller low flow
- g. Basin low-low level
- h. Plant controller failure
- i. Loss of communication with any chiller for more than [60 s]

12.2 **High-priority alarms:**
- a. Plant operating without redundancy
- b. Equipment lockout
- c. Pump or tower fan failure
- d. Sensor failure
- e. Isolation valve position mismatch
- f. FIT-702 and evaporator ΔP disagreement
- g. Idle chiller flow

12.3 **Maintenance alarms:**
- a. Run hours reached
- b. Water treatment alarm
- c. Basin heater failure
- d. Filter ΔP (side-stream filter, if provided)
- e. VFD warnings

---

## 13. Trending

The BAS trends the following at [1 min] intervals, retained [13 months]. Change-of-value trending is used for status points.

13.1 Flow, temperatures and pressures:
- a. FIT-702
- b. CHWST and CHWRT
- c. Active CHWST setpoint
- d. DPT-710, DPT-711 and DPT-712
- e. FCV-701 position

13.2 Pumps and towers:
- a. Speed and status of each pump and fan
- b. CWST and CWRT
- c. OA dry bulb, RH and wet bulb

13.3 Chillers:
- a. Each chiller's %RLA, kW, evaporator and condenser ΔP, entering and leaving temperatures, and alarms

13.4 Calculated values:
- a. Plant tons
- b. kW/ton (with chiller, pump and fan power metering)

13.5 Status and events:
- a. Redundancy status
- b. Reset lockout status
- c. All overrides

---

## 14. Operator Graphics

14.1 **Plant schematic.** Show all points listed above, live, on a plant schematic.

14.2 **Summary displays.** Provide:
- a. A redundancy status banner
- b. Lead/lag table
- c. Run hours
- d. Reset status, including the active lockout reasons
- e. Active overrides
- f. A critical AHU summary showing OR AHU valve position, DAT, dewpoint, and space T/RH

---

## 15. Coordination Items and Assumptions (resolve before bid)

1. **Load vs. firm capacity.** N+1 with three 800-ton chillers gives 1,600 tons of firm capacity. Confirm that the calculated peak plant load, including future growth, is 1,600 tons or less. If it is higher, the plant is not N+1 at peak.

2. **FIT-702 location.** It must measure chiller flow, not system flow (5.4). Confirm on the piping drawings.

3. **Chiller isolation valves.** Because the pumps are headered, each chiller needs automatic evaporator and condenser isolation valves with end switches. These are not listed in the equipment description. Confirm they are provided.

4. **Condenser pump arrangement.** This sequence assumes headered CWPs. If the CWPs are dedicated one-to-one to chillers, simplify Section 7 accordingly. Note that dedicated pumps reduce redundancy flexibility.

5. **Chiller manufacturer data.** Confirm the following:
   - a. Maximum allowable rate of evaporator flow change
   - b. Minimum entering condenser water temperature
   - c. Whether variable condenser flow is acceptable
   - d. Fast-restart capability
   - e. BACnet points list

6. **Second remote DP sensor (DPT-711).** Recommended at the critical surgery AHU, and at any other hydraulically remote critical AHU. A single sensor is a single point of failure for pump control.

7. **CHWST and CHWRT sensors.** Specify matched, calibrated well-mounted sensors, ±0.1°F, for an accurate load calculation.

8. **Tower bypass valve.** Not listed. Recommended for winter operation, because the plant is enabled year-round. Also confirm basin heaters, heat trace, and indoor sump or freeze strategy for your climate.

9. **Emergency power.** Confirm with the electrical engineer:
   - a. Which equipment is on the essential system
   - b. Generator capacity
   - c. Allowable step loads, to finalize the restart stagger (10.5)

10. **Minimum two chillers.** The owner must decide whether to run two chillers during OR hours (3.1). Record the decision in the BOD/OPR.
